title: Asynchronous kernel admission, telemetry, and graceful rewind (WIP)
content:
Context and intent:

This doc collects design notes and an early rollout plan for an asynchronous kernel admission flow that safely enables speculative decoding fast-paths while preserving KV cache coherence and providing clear telemetry to drive acceptance and rollback decisions. The problem space is: how to admit faster kernels (quantized kernels, fused-attention kernels, or 'speculative emitter' kernels) into live traffic for a model family without risking correctness regressions or causing persistent cache divergence across sessions.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Enable progressive admission of new kernels and speculative emitters with minimal latency uplift for most requests.
- Ensure KV cache coherence: no long-lived session divergence after a kernel switch or failed speculative emission.
- Provide crisp telemetry and gates for canary->canary-plus->general rollout phases.
- Support graceful rewind/rollback that can be executed automatically or triggered by ops with minimal user-visible errors.

Design summary (short):
- Admission happens asynchronously: the request path continues on baseline kernel; an admission probe (lightweight) runs in parallel to validate fast kernel output for a small subset of tokens in-memory.
- If probe passes checks, subsequent tokens for the session are switched to the fast kernel; KV handoff uses versioned KV watermarks and ephemeral shadow-caches to detect staleness and reconcile.
- Telemetry captures per-session probe outcomes, kernel-switch rate, early-emission divergence score, KV coherence violations, and user-visible latency/quality metrics.
- Rollback involves (a) immediate traffic steering to baseline kernel, (b) session-level rewind when divergence risk is high, (c) KV cache garbage collection of any ephemeral state.

Architecture and flow (detailed):
1) Admission probe (async):
   - For each incoming session, after initial N tokens (N configurable per-model), start a probe: create a lightweight duplicate of the current context and run the candidate kernel for M probe steps (M small, e.g., 1-4 tokens).
   - Probe runs on lower-priority compute pool or in-situ fast kernel with throttling. It must be rate-limited globally and per-model.
   - Compare outputs using multiple heuristics (see "Probe acceptance checks"). If probe passes, mark session as "eligible" for kernel switchover.

2) Shadow KV and handoff:
   - When a probe runs, it records a shadow KV cache snapshot (not a full copy: store watermark pointer + a hash of last K keys + approximate size).
   - On a successful probe, create an ephemeral overlay KV (ephemeral-shadow) that will be used by the fast kernel. The overlay references the same base store where possible; writes go to overlay until committed.
   - A commit step tries to merge overlay back into base KV atomically at safe watermarks; if merge fails (concurrency/eviction mismatch), surface a coherence violation and treat as failed admission.

3) Kernel switchover contract:
   - Switchover is a session-scoped operation. Contract: either all new tokens post-switch come exclusively from target kernel with overlay; or no switch occurs and baseline continues. Partial switch is disallowed unless a safe rewind is available.
   - Maintain a per-session kernel-version tag and a KV-version watermark. These must be present in traces.

Probe acceptance checks (heuristics):
- Emission distance: top-1 token equality vs baseline for M probe steps. Threshold configurable (e.g., 80% match for first 2 tokens).
- Prob-distribution KL divergence: quick statistical test using first-2 token distributions.
- Safety tokens: if any token among probe outputs matches model-specific safety signal (stop tokens, filter hits), fail probe.
- Latency delta: probe candidate must not exceed per-token latency budget when in admission mode.
- KV coherence dry-run: run overlay merge in sandbox (simulated) to detect eviction/locality mismatches.

Telemetry signals (to collect):
- probe_rate: per-model/week and global.
- probe_success_rate: per-model, per-traffic-tier, time-series.
- kernel_switch_rate: fraction of sessions switched.
- early_emission_agreement: pct top-1/top-3 match in probe.
- kv_overlay_commit_success: commit vs abort ratio.
- kv_coherence_violations: count of detected mismatches (eviction, version mismatch, write collision).
- user_facing_regressions: downstream metrics (QA eval sets, customer complaints, high-level eval scores).
- latency_p95/p99 delta: compare baseline vs sessions switched.
- error_budget_burn: per-model SLO burn tied to kernel admission.

Acceptance gates and rollout criteria (canary -> ramp -> general):
- Canary stage (internal small fraction): probe_rate 100% for canary sessions; switch_rate <= 5%; probe_success_rate >= 95%; kv_overlay_commit_success >= 99%; no kv_coherence_violations for 24h; latency_p99 delta <= 15ms.
- Ramp stage (10-30%): probe_success_rate >= 97%; early_emission_agreement >= 90% on eval prompt set; user_facing_regressions == 0 (no regression alerts); kv_overlay_commit_success >= 99.5%; SLO burn < 10%.
- General stage (>=70%): stable metrics for 72h at previous thresholds; continuous monitoring and auto-fallback policy enabled.

Rollback / graceful rewind plan:
- Triggering conditions: sudden spike in kv_coherence_violations, user_facing_regressions > threshold, latency_p99 delta exceeded, or manual ops decision.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Global switch: route new sessions to baseline kernel (no new admissions).
  2) Session reconciliation: for sessions marked as switched, attempt a best-effort rewind. Options:
     - Fast rewind: replay last safe watermark using baseline kernel for last M tokens; serve new tokens from baseline thereafter. This is preferable when divergence is limited.
     - Hard rewind + rejoin: if divergence is large, terminate session with an explanatory response (graceful failure) and prompt user to restart. Try to preserve partial completions where possible.
  3) Ephemeral overlay cleanup: forcibly GC ephemeral KV overlays older than T_gc threshold.
  4) Postmortem sampling: snapshot a set of affected sessions for full offline analysis.

Operational playbook (ops steps):
- When alert fires (kv_coherence_violations spike):
  - Step 0: Acknowledge in SRE channel and open incident (INF-3421).
  - Step 1: Disable admission globally for affected model family.
  - Step 2: Evaluate top-10 recent sessions for divergence signature.
  - Step 3: If < 1% of sessions affected and rewind succeeds, re-enable with reduced rate and extended telemetry.
  - Step 4: If > 1% or rewind fails, rollback to baseline and schedule hotfix.

Observability and dashboards:
- New dashboard tile: Model Admission Health (per model-version): probe_rate, probe_success_rate, kernel_switch_rate, kv_overlay_commit_success, kv_coherence_violations, latency_p95/p99 delta, user_facing_regressions.
- Tracing: add span tags: kernel.candidate, kernel.base, kv.watermark, session.kernel_tag, admission.probe_id.
- Logs: structured logs for probe decisions (reason codes), overlay commit results, and rewind actions.
- Sampling policy: sample 1% of successful switches for full token trace; 100% of failures must be recorded with context.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Local unit tests: overlay commit merge semantics, watermark arithmetic, probe decision logic.
- Integration tests: simulate eviction races with two concurrent writers to KV; validate coherent outcomes.
- Performance tests: per-model synthetic load to measure latency delta at p50/p95/p99 for both baseline and candidate kernels with overlay.
- Eval harness: run a curated set of 2k prompts per model to compute early_emission_agreement and KL stats pre-rollout.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Cost: probes add compute overhead. We should budget probe CPU/GPU cycles per model family and prioritize high-volume models for non-probe admission gates (i.e., route by policy rather than probe).
- Memory: ephemeral overlay caches increase memory usage per session; cap overlays per-node and implement eviction.
- Kernel API contract: candidate kernels must implement a "dry-run" mode that can run over a snapshot and produce deterministic outputs and a commit-check callback.

Open questions / trade-offs (explicit):
1) How aggressive should probe sampling be for low-traffic models? Tradeoff between cold-start correctness and probe cost.
2) To what extent can we accept partial switch (first tokens from fast kernel then fallback) to reduce latency spikes? Adds complexity for KV coherence.
3) Should we provide a model-level opt-in for admission (i.e., some models permanently excluded)? Implementation complexity vs safety.
4) How to tie admission reversions to automatic retraining or model adjustments?

Short-term action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Priya] Draft minimal probe implementation prototype (single-node) and experimental CLI to run dry-run on sample sessions. (PR: github PR 789)
- [Evan] Instrument trace tags and create Model Admission Health dashboard skeleton.
- [Lina] Prepare eval prompt set + automated agreement script.
- [Marcus] Simulate KV eviction races in staging and produce smoke test scripts.
- [Team] Decide probe default N/M for mid-size LLMs (proposal by 2025-01-10).

Longer-term (Q1):
- Implement atomic overlay commit primitives in runtime; add coherent GC.
- Integrate admission gates into rollout service with canary policies.
- Add automatic rollback detectors tied to SLO burn.

Reference notes / links:
- Related tickets: INF-3421, SERV-1123.
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789
- Example Confluence page (design sketches): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/482915

Appendix: quick checklist for safe rollout (ops playbook condensed):
- Run full eval harness (2k prompts) -> agreement >= threshold
- Canary for 24h with per-minute telemetry guardrails
- KV overlay commit success >= 99% for 24h
- No user-facing regressions flagged by regressions detector
- Smoke-run of rewind procedure on 10 sample sessions

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep admission probe as low friction as possible; product teams hesitate to accept any user-visible rewinds.
- Might need UI/SDK hint for long-running sessions to surface "disclaimer: we may optimize mid-session" — discuss with product.
- Watch for edge-case where tokenization differences between kernels (subtokenization minor differences) cause false divergence.

End of doc.
